title: Parametric Bernstein–von Mises limits and misspecification

items.title: A square-integrable Lipschitz envelope controls a local empirical process
items.statement: For an iid sample and a finite-dimensional parameter ball, a pointwise Lipschitz class with square-integrable envelope has expected centered-process supremum at most C_d r times the envelope's L2 norm on a radius-r ball, and expected modulus at parameter separation epsilon at most C_d epsilon sqrt(log(e r/epsilon)) times that norm. Suprema are interpreted through measurable versions obtained by zero extension off the common full set.
items.strategy: Direct: symmetrize with an independent ghost sample, condition on the observations, and use dyadic Euclidean nets and pair nets with sub-Gaussian Rademacher increments.
items.axiom_use: None. The proof uses finite-dimensional Euclidean nets, finite products, symmetrization, and a square-integrable envelope.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, Lemma 2.1 and proof
Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Lecture 23, QMD and local asymptotic normality

items.title: Compact-uniform LAN and rate contraction imply a total-variation BvM limit
items.statement: Let a finite-dimensional dominated model have an interior point theta-star, a proper prior density continuous and positive near theta-star, and a proper posterior. If the log-likelihood ratio has a compact-uniform LAN expansion at rate delta-n with central vector Delta-n=O_P0(1) and positive-definite quadratic matrix V, and if the posterior contracts in Euclidean parameter norm outside delta-n M-n for every deterministic M-n tending to infinity, then the posterior law of delta-n^{-1}(theta-theta-star) is o_P0(1) in the event-supremum total-variation distance from N_d(V^{-1}Delta-n,V^{-1}). The result is conditional on the stated rate-contraction premise.
items.strategy: Direct: prove tightness of the scaled posterior from the every-diverging-radius contraction premise, compare the posterior and Gaussian laws after conditioning on a fixed compact ball, then remove the tails.
items.axiom_use: AC is used only for the library multivariate-normal-law construction and, when a supplied density family is not already part of the data, the selected likelihood-density convention. The proof itself uses the explicitly supplied jointly measurable density family.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, Theorem 2.1 and proof
A. W. van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics, Chapter 10, §10.2, Theorem 10.1 and proof

items.title: The QMD route uses normalized absolutely continuous likelihoods and a separate uniform LAN premise
items.statement: Assume AC and a common-dominator iid QMD path at an interior theta-star with P0=P_theta-star. For u=h/sqrt(n), let alpha(u)=P_theta-star+u(p_theta-star=0) and normalize the alternative density on {p_theta-star>0} by 1-alpha(u). If the normalized absolutely continuous component has a compact-uniform LAN expansion, the prior is continuous and positive at theta-star, and the posterior has the parameter-rate contraction required by the general BvM theorem, then that theorem applies. QMD controls the singular and zero-overlap masses and makes the full product law total-variation close to the normalized absolutely continuous component; the existing fixed-local-sequence QMD-LAN theorem alone does not assert compact-uniform LAN.
items.strategy: Direct: bound the one-observation singular mass uniformly on compact local directions, compare the actual posterior likelihood ratio with the normalized absolutely continuous component on the base-law support, and then invoke the LAN-to-BvM theorem under the separate compact-uniform premise.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the singular/zero-overlap mass, normalized-product, fixed-sequence LAN, and LAN-to-BvM suppliers, including their Gaussian-law dependencies. The jointly measurable density versions are supplied, so no choice of versions is made here; def-qmd-path asserts no choice principle. The proof does not assert a full Radon–Nikodym derivative for the whole local alternative.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Lecture 23, QMD and local asymptotic normality
B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, §2.1

items.title: A local KL expansion and square-integrable log-Lipschitz envelope give misspecified iid LAN
items.statement: For iid data from P0 in a jointly measurable dominated density model, suppose theta-star is an interior finite KL minimizer, the log density is differentiable in P0-probability at theta-star, nearby log-density ratios have a common square-integrable Lipschitz envelope, and the KL contrast has a positive-definite second-order expansion there. Then the iid log-likelihood ratio has LAN uniformly on every compact set at rate n^{-1/2}, with central vector V^{-1} n^{-1/2} sum_i score(X_i). The score is square-integrable and P0-centered; no equality between score covariance and V is asserted. Empirical suprema use measurable versions on the common log-Lipschitz full set.
items.strategy: Direct: derive score centering and square integrability from differentiability plus the envelope, bound the centered remainder by the local empirical-process lemma, and use the second-order KL expansion for the deterministic term.
items.axiom_use: None. A supplied jointly measurable density family is part of the hypotheses; the score, LAN expansion, and probability bounds are proved without selecting new density versions or applying a choice-dependent central limit theorem.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, §2.2, Lemma 2.1 and proof
Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Lecture 23, QMD and local asymptotic normality

items.title: Misspecified iid LAN gives a BvM limit when the posterior has the required parameter rate
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the misspecified iid LAN theorem, add a prior density continuous and positive at theta-star, proper finite evidence, and posterior contraction outside n^{-1/2} M-n in parameter norm for every deterministic M-n tending to infinity. Then the scaled posterior is o_P0(1) in total variation from N_d(V^{-1}Delta-n,V^{-1}). The rate-contraction condition remains an explicit premise and is not inferred from ordinary posterior consistency at a KL projection.
items.strategy: Direct: apply the iid LAN result to supply the uniform likelihood expansion and apply the general LAN-to-BvM theorem with the stated prior and posterior-tail hypotheses.
items.axiom_use: Inherits only the AC assumption of the LAN-to-BvM theorem's multivariate-normal target. No additional axiom is used.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, Theorems 2.1 and Lemma 2.1
A. W. van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics, Chapter 10, §10.2, Theorem 10.1 and proof

items.title: A consistent approximate MLE has the misspecified sandwich limit under local LAN conditions
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of the misspecified iid LAN theorem and AC. If a measurable estimator theta-hat-n is consistent for theta-star and its empirical average log likelihood is within o_P0(n^{-1}) of the global supremum, then sqrt(n)(theta-hat-n-theta-star)=V^{-1} n^{-1/2} sum_i score(X_i)+o_P0(1), with sampling covariance V^{-1} I V^{-1}, where I=P0[score score^T]. Under the posterior rate-contraction premise of the LAN-to-BvM theorem, the posterior can also be centered at sqrt(n)(theta-hat-n-theta-star) in the same total-variation limit. The consistency and approximate-maximization conditions are separate assumptions; no MLE consistency claim is made here.
items.strategy: Direct: use the local empirical-process bound and positive KL curvature to prove root-n tightness by dyadic shells, optimize the uniform LAN quadratic, then apply the multivariate CLT and a Gaussian location-shift bound.
items.axiom_use: AC is used for the multivariate iid CLT and library Gaussian laws. The exact uses are the score-sum limit and the normal comparison law; no AC is used to obtain MLE consistency.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, Lemma 2.2 and proof conditions
Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Lecture 23, maximum likelihood conditions under QMD

title: Parametric Bernstein–von Mises limits and misspecification — Examples

items.title: A correctly specified regular normal mean model
items.statement: For X_i iid N(theta-star,1), a proper N(0,tau^2) prior gives an exact normal posterior whose sqrt(n)-scaled law is within o_P(1) total variation of N(sqrt(n)(bar X-theta-star),1); the posterior and sampling widths both tend to n^{-1/2}.
items.strategy: Verification: complete the square in the normal likelihood times prior, rescale the exact posterior, and bound the location and scale changes in total variation.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics, Chapter 10, §10.2
B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, §1 and §2.1

items.title: A unit-variance normal working model can miscalibrate credible intervals
items.statement: Under a dominated iid truth with mean zero and finite variance sigma^2>0, the N(theta,1) working likelihood has expected-log-likelihood maximizer theta-star=0 (and KL projection when the directional KL is finite), exact posterior width asymptotic to n^{-1/2}, and sampling width sigma n^{-1/2}; central posterior intervals have limiting coverage 2 Phi(z_{1-alpha/2}/sigma)-1.
items.strategy: Verification: normalize the Gaussian prior, complete the square in the working likelihood, identify the exact posterior width and MLE, and apply the iid CLT to the truth's sample mean.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, Example 2.1
Natalia Bochkina, Bernstein-von Mises theorem and misspecified models: a review, §§1.2 and 1.4

items.title: At a boundary, the normal posterior limit is truncated
items.statement: For the normal mean model restricted to theta>=0, truth theta-star=0, and an exponential prior, the sqrt(n)-scaled posterior is a normal law truncated to [0,infinity); its total-variation distance from the untruncated Gaussian LAN approximation stays bounded away from zero with nonvanishing probability.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the exact truncated posterior after rescaling and use the negative half-line as a total-variation witness for the untruncated Gaussian approximation.

references.title: Natalia Bochkina, Bernstein-von Mises theorem and misspecified models: a review, §1.4.1
